facts:
## CELL FACTS

Cell 火_正官 (Fire carrying The Magistrate). Persona The Magistrate (正官). Definition line: "Framework-mediated pressure, the standard that steadies". Keyword Order, charge gentle, poles catalyst Integrity / friction Rigidity. Family function: Order. Cost dimension: the standard that steadies; the frame that holds you holds you in. Arena: the gate, the seal, order, the appointed hour. Classical portrait: framework-mediated pressure; the standard that steadies; rank held by rules, rigidity as the shadow. Ruled domains: Career, Status, Order. Sibling (other polarity of the family): 七杀.
Element arena: Fire (flame, light, warmth, fuel, the hearth, the blaze). dm_element (which core reads this cell): Metal. structural_interaction seed: "Fire setting standard for Metal cross-polarity — the forge that refines and grants recognition".
- k2_overview: "Your Fire moves as the Magistrate: civic light, authority that illuminates. You carry rules the way lighthouses carry flame, visibly, warmly, for everyone’s navigation. People follow your lead because it brightens rather than binds. Office becomes you. Keep the light public and tended, and rank will keep arriving on its own."
- k2_functional: "You carry order like a lantern: visible standards others steer by, kept lit at personal cost."
- adj_chips: {"friction":["Rule-bound","Afraid to slip","Never says no"],"catalyst":"[REDACTED: the words under test]"}
- k2_domain_readings: {"Career":"Your career runs on visible service: roles where leading and lighting are the same act. Teaching, governance, the public face of good systems. Seek podiums attached to substance.","Status":"Your standing is luminous and watched: warmth draws the credit and the scrutiny together. Live as if lit, because you are. The honest glow survives every inspection.","Order":"Your order is inspirational: people comply because you made the rule glow with purpose. That is rare governance. Write things down too. Light needs a lamp when you leave."}
- fn_reading.catalyst.ledger (three rows, index-aligned to adj_chips.catalyst; authored order is significance order):
  - row 0: [REDACTED: the target row]
  - row 1: [REDACTED: the target row]
  - row 2: [REDACTED: the target row]
- Sibling cell 火_七杀 chips (nothing you write may fit the sibling): {"catalyst":["Clear under pressure","Takes charge","Loves high stakes"],"friction":["Hard on yourself","Pushes too hard","Never off duty"]}
- Sibling cell 火_七杀 catalyst row 0 drive passage, for the sibling test on the tension (this row must name a different either-or): "Pressure is where your thinking gets clear. Since you need certainty more than comfort, you let outside pressure clear your head rather than make your own calm. Choose some of that pressure yourself, because you are only this clear with something at stake."

Core element Metal, energy element Fire. Law: Fire tames Metal (火克金: the forge softens the blade). Relative to the core the energy is the tamer, so Fire is this core's Order. No chart is attached to this batch: the cell is written for every chart with a Metal core that shows Fire on the catalyst pole, so no percentage and no state of one chart appears in any value. The catalyst pole of Fire as the Order is the Overfueled band's case (the core has more than it channels); tone by pole: compliment. Rows: row 0, row 1, row 2, each with its three angles (drive, cost_self, cost_others: the drive, the cost to the reader, the cost to others; the app shows one angle per row by position rotation, so each passage must stand alone); one chip per row, written once and copied byte-identical onto the row's three fields. The pair cell 金_火's definition and advice for this pole are rewritten in the same batch (the pair skeleton) and are withheld here; no four-word run may be shared with them, so keep every phrase the ledger's own.

value.text: Every promise you make becomes a rule you keep. Being relied on is the closest you get to feeling safe, so you keep your word ahead of your freedom to change it. Promise a little less freely, because you keep every one you make.

value_b.text: You treat every promise as a contract with a witness. Since an outside standard keeps you steady, you keep the promise as much as the person you made it to. Reopen one promise a year, because you keep it long after it stops fitting.

value.text: Keeping a promise costs you the right to change your mind. You would rather keep a stale promise than break it, so you stay inside plans past their use. Let yourself out of one, because you turn down better offers to keep old promises.

value.text: By the book is the only way you trust a thing done. Since an outside rule steadies you, you go by the book ahead of the shortcut. Stay with the book, because you are the standard the work gets checked against.

value_b.text: You feel most at home going by the book. Because an old rule holds you steady, you go the long way by the book rather than around it. Trust the book's slow route, since you are built for a standing that lasts.

value.text: Where the book and your judgment part, you side with the book. You want it done in order more than your way, so you let the book decide what you knew. Allow the book one exception, because you give up chances that cannot wait.

value.text: A fairly earned title is worth more to you than any praise. Since an earned rank says you belong, you earn the next title ahead of chasing the next thrill. Let the title come slowly, because you are already doing the job it names.

value_b.text: You want a title earned in full before enjoying it. Because you believe only a rank with work behind it, you take the title in writing over the thanks in passing. Enjoy the thanks too, since you earned it long ahead of the paperwork.

value.text: Earning the title comes first, claiming it long after. You want to look deserving more than to be paid, so you earn it twice before asking once. Claim it now, because earning it this slowly leaves money you were owed on the table.

value.text: Where titles are concerned, you make everyone earn theirs too. Since an unearned rank looks like cheating, you give a colleague the long route rather than a quiet word. Say the word sometimes, because you take from them the years that earning costs.
